headline: The U.S. Servicemember arrested earlier this week by Counter Terrorism Policing in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia, has been identified as 41-year-old Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, a senior human resources officer stationed at NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC) headquarters in Gloucestershire, England and an 18-year veteran of the U.S. Army. Tyner’s arrest was the result of a string operation following a lengthy investigation by the UK Metropolitan Police Service, MI5, U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command and FBI, with him expected to be formally charged by British authorities on Sunday or Monday, officials tell NBC News. Official state that at the time of his arrest, Tyner had not yet handed over any information to Moscow. He is expected to be turned over to American authorities after being charged in the UK, with the intention of being tried by the U.S. Army under the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ). Tyner previously served in high-profile roles during deployments to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar.
